purpose: Per-stage executed evidence for the one case the wave-17 CT lane mapped on the existing legacy_c route, written in the same shape as docs/reports/wave9-ctwin/ct_stage_evidence.json so scripts/ct_stage_summary.py merges it with the earlier per-card records.
derivation_rule: A stage is `executed` only where a named workspace test runs it on the case's own artifact. A control with its own source is executed on THAT artifact and is therefore not one of this case's observations; a control that varies only the declared contracts re-analyzes the case's own bytes and would be (card CT-CTWIN), and CT40 carries none of that kind.
route: legacy_c (qcore_c_gateway::legacy_c::validate_unrestricted_c11 then analyze_unrestricted_c11, reached through the public qcore_compiler reexports). The gateway is unedited by this lane: `git diff` over crates/ and compiler/src/ is empty.
why_this_case_maps_now: Card CT-CTWIN measured CT40 in wave 9 and left it unmapped because publish-then-free was Safe with no diagnostic: neither the verdict class the scenario demands nor a construct to attribute it to. Card CTWIN-PUBLISH (wave 16) reproduced that hazard and closed it at the general gateway site, refusing a store of a tracked identity into an object that outlives the call. Both halves of the wave-9 attribution rule now hold on this tree, re-measured on this lane's own fixture bytes before the manifest was edited.
what_the_mapping_does_not_claim: The mapping rests on the construct CT40's `expected` text names — the lifetime/publication protocol — and explicitly not on the two things its title names. `_Atomic` is measured non-load-bearing (the plain_pointer.c control is byte-identical in verdict, reason, statuses and ordered diagnostics), and `prematurely freed` is not decided either (the no_release.c control publishes without any release and is still refused). Both are pinned as fixture controls so the bound is structural rather than a sentence in a report.
lean_is_not_applicable: Judged not applicable on the same grounds cards T00-CT-SCHEMA, T08-SRC-CT, CT-CTWIN and the wave-11/wave-13 CT lanes recorded: this lane adds no checker rule, no diagnostic code, no lowering and no model. It adds one fixture, three manifest/harness pins and one derived-mechanism extension over an unedited gateway whose 30 publication theorems landed with card CTWIN-PUBLISH. `proof` stays `unassessed` for CT40; no theorem is bound to any CT fixture (T00.7 remains open).
no_native_or_sanitized_evidence_added: The legacy_c route has no c_emission stage, so it has nothing to sanitize and nothing to run: native_execution and native_sanitized are structurally not_applicable, exactly as for CT43 and CT45. Harness-gated sanitized-native evidence stays at CT03/CT17/CT26/CT34 — 4 of 33 rather than 4 of 32 — and proof stays 0 of 33. The denominator grew by mapping, not by conformance.

CT41.re_measured_on_this_tree: Three shapes over the q_* surface: a `volatile int` completion flag beside an acquisition and release, the same body with a plain `int`, and the body with no flag at all. The first two are byte-identical — unknown, reason `resource projection unresolved: 1 unsupported operation(s), 1 unresolved alias(es), 0 custody summary conflict(s)`, `[subject:4:unknown-alias:p, subject:4:unsupported:unsupported assignment expression]` — and the third is safe with no diagnostic. The qualifier moves nothing; the store does.
CT41.why_still_unmapped: The recorded blocker is accurate and is now a decision rather than a gap. Card CTWIN-PUBLISH §5 asserts the invariance as correct: C11 `volatile` is an access-ordering qualifier for the abstract machine, not a synchronization primitive (§5.1.2.4 gives happens-before to atomics, mutexes and thread creation/join only), so a projection that derives no synchronization fact MUST answer identically with and without it — answering differently would be the defect. No verdict of this gateway is therefore evidence about a synchronization proof, and a mapping would be vacuous under clause (b) of the wave-9 attribution rule.
CT41.follow_on: CT-CTWIN-SYNC (decided by card CTWIN-PUBLISH §5, not open as a gap)

CT42.scenario: Two descriptors share an underlying logical state
CT42.re_measured_on_this_tree: The contract loader still refuses an int-typed owned result verbatim: `contracts.qcore: q_open_fd at byte 18: owned result requires a pointer return type`. The descriptor twin without such a contract is unknown on three uncontracted calls (`q_close_fd`, `q_dup_fd`, `q_open_fd`). The pointer-alias analogue — `void *b = a;` then two releases — is a provisional unsafe with one `double-release` diagnostic, which is a syntactic alias surviving, a different question from a preserved protocol-cell identity.
CT42.why_still_unmapped: The case asks for a preserved identity, a positive modelling property, and no verdict measured here establishes one; its Unknown says only that the projection cannot express descriptors. Unchanged from card CT-CTWIN's measurement, re-verified rather than inherited.

unmapped_reasons_provenance: CT41 and CT42 keep the bucket card CT-CTWIN measured — `blocked-on-gateway-expressiveness (C-twin measured)` — so neither row declares a supersession: re-verification reaching the same label is the record saying the label still holds. Only the reasons move, and only for CT41, whose blocker CTWIN-PUBLISH converted from an open question into an asserted decision. Inventing a new bucket for that would be label churn without a measurement to justify it, and the tally shape would move for a case nothing about which moved. CT40's row is not repeated here: the case is mapped, so it has no blocker to publish, and the wave-9 record's row for it is retired below rather than deleted from that record.
